extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent owners, third-party requesters, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and filing (and understanding the processing of) a request for ex parte reexamination of a U.S. patent under 35 U.S.C. 301–307 and 37 CFR 1.510, including required content, fees, timing, representation, and procedural consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of citation on patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of any submission of a citation of prior art patents or printed publications in a patent file should be served on the patent owner so that the patent owner is kept fully informed as to the content of his or her patent file wrapper (/file history/).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service should be addressed to the correspondence address set forth in 37 CFR 1.33(c). See MPEP § 2206 and § 2222 for handling of prior art citations and correspondence addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file (any person)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may, at any time during the period of enforceability of a patent, file a request for an ex parte reexamination by the Office of any claim of the patent on the basis of prior art patents or printed publications (37 CFR 1.510).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No persons are excluded; corporations and governmental entities included. The patent owner may also request reexamination; the Director may initiate reexamination on limited basis. The name of the requester will not be maintained in confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for requesting (period of enforceability)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request may be filed at any time during the period of enforceability of the patent (37 CFR 1.510(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office's rule defines the period of enforceability (e.g., adding 6 years to the patent expiration date and accounting for maintenance fees, disclaimers, term extensions or adjustments). Litigation instituted within the statute of limitations may affect timing; requests may sometimes be filed after statute expiration if patent remains enforceable against someone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intent and objectives of reexamination procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The intent includes: (A) to provide procedures for reexamination of patents; (B) to implement reexamination in an essentially ex parte manner; (C) to minimize processing costs and complexities; (D) to maximize respect for the reexamined patent; (E) to provide procedures for prompt and timely determinations in accordance with the 'special dispatch' requirements of 35 U.S.C. 305.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These policy goals guide how reexamination proceedings are processed and prioritized by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic characteristics of ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Characteristics include: (A) anyone can request reexamination during enforceability; (B) prior art considered is limited to patents or printed publications under 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103; (C) a substantial new question of patentability (SNQ) must be present to order reexamination; (D) if ordered, proceeding is ex parte in nature; (E) decision on the request must be made no later than 3 months from filing, with remainder of proceedings proceeding with 'special dispatch'; (F) normally conducted to conclusion and issuance of a reexamination certificate; (G) scope of a claim cannot be enlarged by amendment; (H) all reexamination and patent files are open to the public; (I) reexamination file is scanned into IFW and public access is via PAIR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the core constraints and procedural expectations for ex parte reexamination (e.g., timeframes, scope of prior art, public access, claim amendment limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request must be in writing and accompanied by fee
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for ex parte reexamination must be in writing and must be accompanied by payment of a reexamination fee established by the Director pursuant to section 41 (37 CFR 1.510 and MPEP § 2215).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The entire fee required under 37 CFR 1.20(c)(1) must be paid for the request to be accepted, given a filing date, and published in the Official Gazette. If the fee is not paid, the request may be treated as a citation in the patent file if it otherwise complies with § 1.501(a). Refunds are available if reexamination is denied or vacated (see 37 CFR 1.26(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of request — required elements (37 CFR 1.510(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for reexamination must include: (1) a statement pointing out each substantial new question of patentability based on prior patents and printed publications; (2) identification of every claim for which reexamination is requested and a detailed explanation of the pertinency and manner of applying the cited prior art to every claim (and, if appropriate, how claims distinguish over cited prior art); (3) a copy of every patent or printed publication relied upon accompanied by English translations of necessary parts of non‑English documents; (4) a copy of the entire patent (front face, drawings, specification/claims) in double column format, with each page plainly written on only one side; (5) a certification that a copy of the request filed by a person other than the patent owner has been served in its entirety on the patent owner at the address in § 1.33(c), with name and address of party served (or duplicate copy supplied if service not possible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement of SNQ should clearly point out why reexamination is warranted. Cited prior art should be listed on a Form PTO-1449/PTO/SB/08A/08B or equivalent. Copies and translations are required so the examiner can fully consider materials. The request should apply the cited prior art to every claim requested; requesters may not argue the references do not raise an SNQ in the request itself (i.e., the request must assert an SNQ). If the patent owner files no statement under 37 CFR 1.530(b), then the requester cannot file later replies under 1.535.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of cited prior art to claims (pertinency/manner)
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must include 'a detailed explanation of the pertinency and manner of applying the cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested' and may point out how claims distinguish over cited prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters should explicitly apply each cited reference to each claim; if the requester is the patent owner, they may indicate distinctions. The request should be as complete as possible because the examiner may not consider other prior art when deciding whether to institute reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies and translations requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of every patent or printed publication relied upon must be supplied, accompanied by an English language translation of all necessary and pertinent parts of any non-English language patent or printed publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translations of at least the portions relied upon are required so the examiner can perform full consideration. See MPEP § 2218 for handling translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent copy formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the entire patent including front face, drawings, and specification/claims (in double column format) must be provided, and all copies must have each page plainly written on only one side of a sheet of paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Printed patent pages should be reproduced as they appear in the printed patent. Two-sided copies are not proper. Any disclaimers, certificates of correction, or reexamination certificates that are part of the patent must also be supplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of service on patent owner (if requester is not owner)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request is filed by a person other than the patent owner, a certification that a copy of the request has been served in its entirety on the patent owner at the address in § 1.33(c) must be included, indicating the name and address of the party served; if service was not possible, a duplicate copy must be supplied to the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certification must set forth the name and address used to serve the patent owner and date of service. Failure to properly certify service may affect processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of the request is either (1) the date on which the request including the entire fee is received in the Patent and Trademark Office, or (2) the date on which the last portion of the fee for requesting reexamination is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the fee is not paid, the request is incomplete; the requester is notified and given opportunity to complete. If the fee remains unpaid, no determination is made and the papers may be placed in the patent file as a citation if they meet § 1.501(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling incomplete requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If the request does not include the fee or all required parts, the identified requester will be notified and given an opportunity to complete the request within a specified time. If not corrected, the Office will make the determination on the request as it then exists (if fee paid) or will not make a determination (if fee unpaid).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fee paid but defects not corrected in time, decision is based on the request as filed. If fee unpaid and defects not corrected, request papers are ordinarily placed in the patent file as a prior art citation (see § 2206).

rubrics_metrics.name: No withdrawal/abandonment after filing with fee
rubrics_metrics.description: After the request for reexamination, including the entire fee for requesting reexamination, is received in the Office, no abandonment, withdrawal, or striking of the request is possible, regardless of who requests the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In limited circumstances (e.g., final court decision where all claims finally held invalid), a reexamination order may be vacated (see MPEP § 2286).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed amendment by patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: A request filed by the patent owner may include a proposed amendment in accordance with 37 CFR 1.530.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner files a proposed amendment, excess claims fees under 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (c)(4) may also apply. See MPEP § 2250.03 for excess claims fee issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative authority and correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request is filed by an attorney or agent identifying another party on whose behalf the request is being filed, the attorney or agent must have a power of attorney from that party or be acting in a representative capacity pursuant to § 1.34(a) (37 CFR 1.510(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Processing of the reexamination request will not be delayed due to absence of filing of power of attorney, but proof of authority may be required if authority is questioned. All correspondence for a requester who is not the patent owner should be addressed to the requester's representative unless specified otherwise. A patent owner may not be represented by someone not registered to practice before the Office for signing amendments or other papers in a reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of prior art considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art considered during reexamination is limited to prior art patents or printed publications applied under the appropriate parts of 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matters such as prior public use or on-sale may not be considered in ex parte reexamination; patent owner seeking broader issues may file a reissue application instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial New Question (SNQ) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office initially determines if 'a substantial new question of patentability' (35 U.S.C. 303(a)) is presented; a request must assert a substantial new question of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement of SNQ should clearly point out what the requester considers to be the SNQ and list cited prior art on the appropriate form. A requester may not argue, in the request, that the submitted references do not raise an SNQ and that no order should be issued—the request must assert the SNQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframe and 'special dispatch' processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision on the request must be made no later than 3 months from its filing, and the remainder of proceedings must proceed with 'special dispatch' within the Office (35 U.S.C. 305).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ordered, reexamination proceedings are given expedited processing and normally proceed to issuance of a reexamination certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access and electronic file availability
rubrics_metrics.description: All reexamination and patent files are open to the public; the reexamination file is scanned into IFW to provide an electronic format copy available through PAIR. Any remaining paper files are not available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public access and copying should be made from the electronic copy available via PAIR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Form PTO/SB/57 (PTO-1465) transmittal
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/57 is a Request for Ex Parte Reexamination Transmittal Form (also referred to as FORM PTO-1465) and its use as transmittal/cover is encouraged but not required by law or rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form lists the items to include (fee, patent copy, copies of cited references, translations, certification of service, correspondence address, concurrent proceedings, etc.). Warnings: information on the form may become public; do not include credit card info on the form (use PTO-2038 for credit card). Use of the form can assist in assembling required elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness and examiner consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The request should be as complete as possible, since there is no guarantee the examiner will consider other prior art when making the decision on the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because no later reply by the requester may be permitted if the patent owner files no statement under 37 CFR 1.530(b), thoroughness at filing is important.
